title: Best Cat Litter Boxes 2026: Top Picks for Every Cat
description: A good litter box keeps your home clean and your cat happy. The wrong one can lead to messes, odors, and even behavioral issues where your cat refuses to use...
content:
Why the Right Litter Box Matters

A good litter box keeps your home clean and your cat happy. The wrong one can lead to messes, odors, and even behavioral issues where your cat refuses to use it.

Let's start with the stat that should drive every purchase decision here: according to the American Veterinary Medical Association, inappropriate elimination — a cat peeing or pooping outside the box — is consistently one of the top behavioral reasons cats are surrendered to shelters. The AVMA's guidance is blunt: litter box problems are usually a box problem, not a cat problem, and most can be fixed by matching the box to what the cat actually wants.

What do cats actually want in 2026? The same things they've always wanted: a box at least 1.5 times their body length, clean litter, a quiet spot away from food and foot traffic, and one more box than the number of cats in the house. What's changed is the product landscape. The Litter-Robot 4 and its competitors have made automatic boxes genuinely reliable rather than novelty items, and the newer high-sided pans like the Petmate Giant have largely solved the litter-scatter problem that drove owners crazy a decade ago.

Two rules I give every cat owner, and they cost nothing: scoop daily (a box scooped once a day gets used; a box scooped weekly gets avoided), and put the box somewhere the cat can see approaches coming — cats hate being ambushed while they're vulnerable. A covered box in a corner with one entrance is a trap from your cat's point of view.

What to Look For

  • Size: Should be 1.5x your cat's length
  • Depth: Enough for 2-3 inches of litter
  • Entry: Low enough for easy access
  • Covered vs Open: Depends on your cat's preference

Top 5 Cat Litter Boxes

cat litter boxes

1. Litter-Robot 4 - Best Automatic

Self-cleaning litter box that sifts waste automatically. Expensive but saves time. Litter-Robot 4 on Amazon. If you're away from home a lot, the convenience is real — it keeps the litter clean between scoopings, which is exactly what a picky cat needs. See our full self-cleaning litter box guide for the alternatives.

Pros: Automatic cleaning, odor control, app connectivity

Cons: Expensive, needs power outlet

2. Petmate Giant Litter Pan - Best Value

Extra-large open pan at an affordable price. Simple but effective. Petmate Giant Litter Pan on Amazon.

Pros: Large size, affordable, easy to clean

3. Modkat Flip Litter Box - Best Covered

Modern design with flip-top lid. Includes scoop and reusable liner. Modkat Flip on Amazon. The flip-top design makes scooping dramatically easier than the old lift-the-whole-hood approach, and the liner system cuts down on scrubbing.

Pros: Stylish, reduces tracking, easy to fill

4. Nature's Miracle High-Sided - Best for Kickers

High sides prevent litter scatter. Non-stick surface for easy cleaning. If your cat digs like it's looking for buried treasure, this is the box that keeps the litter in the box. Nature's Miracle High-Sided on Amazon.

5. Catit Jumbo Hooded - Best for Large Cats

Extra-large hooded box perfect for Maine Coons and other big breeds. A hooded box traps odor and gives a private feel, but only if the interior is big enough — a Maine Coon in a standard hooded box will simply refuse it.

Tips for Success

  • One box per cat, plus one extra
  • Place in quiet, accessible location
  • Scoop daily, deep clean weekly
  • Replace box every 1-2 years (plastic absorbs odors)

On the scooping front, the ASPCA's behavioral guidance matches what the AVMA says: scoop at least once daily, and if you're using clumping litter, top it up rather than dumping it all — most cats prefer consistent litter depth of 2-3 inches. And don't use strongly scented litter; cats have a far more sensitive sense of smell than we do, and "fresh scent" to a human can be "chemical assault" to a cat. Our cat litter buying guide breaks down clumping, clay, silica, and the odor-control claims.

Conclusion

cat litter boxes

For most cats, the Petmate Giant Litter Pan offers the best value. For automatic cleaning, the Litter-Robot 4 is worth the investment. Always choose a size larger than you think you need.

And if your cat has already started avoiding the box, go back to basics before you buy anything new: add a second box, move it somewhere quiet, and scoop daily for two weeks. In my experience, that combination resolves the majority of litter box problems without spending a cent. If it doesn't, a vet visit is the right next step — medical issues like urinary tract infections are a common hidden cause of inappropriate elimination. Our litter mat guide and deodorizer guide cover the cleanup side of things.

title: Best Fish Food for Tropical Fish 2026: Complete Guide
description: Tropical fish require varied diets to maintain vibrant colors and good health. Different species have different needs - some are herbivores, others carnivore…
content:
Feeding Tropical Fish

Tropical fish require varied diets to maintain vibrant colors and good health. Different species have different needs - some are herbivores, others carnivores, and many are omnivores.

The 2026 feeding picture is better than it's ever been, mostly because the food itself got better. Insect-protein foods like Fluval Bug Bites went from niche to mainstream, and the big flake brands responded by pushing protein content up and fillers out. The result: you can now feed a genuinely complete diet from off-the-shelf foods without supplementing, as long as you rotate. I keep a staple flake, a sinking pellet for the bottom-dwellers, and frozen bloodworms or brine shrimp in the freezer for a few times a week — that trio covers virtually every community tank.

One thing to be careful about: "color enhancing" doesn't mean "better." Foods like Omega One Super Color use natural pigments from salmon and shrimp, which is fine. Cheap flakes that promise intense color often just add dyes that do nothing for the fish. Read the ingredient list — the first ingredients should be actual protein sources, not wheat or corn meal. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration requires pet food labels, including fish food, to show a guaranteed analysis of nutrients, and checking that crude protein and fat numbers are actually listed is the fastest way to spot a low-quality flake.

On feeding amounts, the standard advice is still right: feed only what the fish can eat in 2-3 minutes, once or twice a day, and fast the tank one day a week. Overfeeding is the single most common cause of water quality problems in new tanks, and it's entirely preventable. If you're feeding more than a pinch per fish per meal, you're probably overfeeding. The RSPCA's fish care guidance echoes this directly — it lists overfeeding and poor water quality as the two most common causes of illness in pet fish, and both are owner-controlled.

Feeding Guidelines

  • Feed 2-3 times daily
  • Only what they can eat in 2-3 minutes
  • Variety is key - rotate foods
  • Fast one day per week (aids digestion)

Top 5 Tropical Fish Foods

fish food tropical fish

1. TetraMin Plus Tropical Flakes - Best Overall

Classic tropical flakes with added vitamins and color enhancers. Suitable for most community fish. TetraMin Plus on Amazon.

Pros: Nutritionally complete, doesn't cloud water

2. Hikari Micro Pellets - Best for Small Fish

Tiny pellets perfect for tetras, rasboras, and other small tropicals. Hikari Micro Pellets on Amazon.

3. Fluval Bug Bites - Natural Option

Made with insect protein for a natural diet. Great for finicky eaters. Fluval Bug Bites on Amazon. Insect protein is closer to what many tropicals eat in the wild than fish meal, and most fish go for it immediately — it's the food I recommend for picky eaters first.

4. Omega One Super Color - For Vibrant Colors

High in protein with natural color enhancers from salmon and shrimp. Omega One Super Color on Amazon. The whole-flake processing keeps more nutrients intact than the high-heat extrusion used for some pellets.

5. New Life Spectrum Thera+A - Premium Choice

High-quality pellets with garlic for immune support. Excellent for sensitive fish. The garlic is a genuine appetite stimulant and immune supporter, and it's the food most experienced keepers reach for when a fish is recovering from illness.

Food Types Explained

  • Flakes: Surface feeders, most common
  • Pellets: Sinking or floating, less waste
  • Frozen: Brine shrimp, bloodworms - great treat
  • Freeze-dried: Convenient alternative to frozen
  • Live: Best for conditioning breeders

One caution on freeze-dried foods: they're a great convenience, but they should be soaked before feeding or they can cause bloat and digestive issues in fish that gulp them dry. Drop them in a cup of tank water for a minute first — it takes seconds and prevents a real problem. The frozen and freeze-dried food guide covers the details.

Feeding Tips

fish food tropical fish

  • Remove uneaten food after 5 minutes
  • Soak dry food before feeding (prevents bloat)
  • Match food size to fish mouth size
  • Use automatic feeder when away

If you're heading out of town, an automatic feeder set to a light schedule beats asking a neighbor to feed the tank — well-meaning neighbors consistently overfeed. And before you travel, do a water change and test the water so the tank starts the week in good shape.

Conclusion

For most tropical community tanks, TetraMin Plus Flakes is a great staple. Add variety with Frozen bloodworms or Fluval Bug Bites. Avoid overfeeding - it's the #1 cause of water quality issues.

If you want to dig deeper into what each species actually needs, our full aquarium fish food guide has species-specific breakdowns, and the bottom feeder food guide covers sinking pellets and wafers for catfish and loaches. And remember — no food fixes bad water. If your fish look off, test the water before you change the menu; our fish disease guide explains why most problems trace back to water quality.

title: Best Dog Toys for Aggressive Chewers 2026
description: Some dogs can destroy any toy in minutes. If you have a German Shepherd, Pit Bull, Golden Retriever, or any powerful chewer, you know the frustration of buyi…
content:
Why Aggressive Chewers Need Special Toys

Some dogs can destroy any toy in minutes. If you have a German Shepherd, Pit Bull, Golden Retriever, or any powerful chewer, you know the frustration of buying "durable" toys that don't last a day. Aggressive chewers need toys specifically designed to withstand powerful jaws.

Source: American Kennel Club (AKC): The AKC advises that most adult dogs require a minimum of 30 minutes to 2 hours of structured physical activity daily, with working and sporting breeds often needing significantly more. Chewing is a natural outlet for that energy, and the AKC notes that destructive chewing in adult dogs is frequently a sign of under-exercise rather than stubbornness.

One thing changed in 2026: the best heavy-duty toys now come with published bite-force and durability testing. KONG publishes its rubber durometer specs, West Paw backs its toys with a one-time replacement guarantee, and Goughnuts literally prints a wear indicator into the rubber so you know when the toy has done its job. That's a big upgrade from the days when "indestructible" just meant "thick." It matters, because no toy is actually indestructible — the good ones just fail safely, in chunks too big to swallow, instead of splintering into bits your dog can choke on.

Before you buy anything, one rule of thumb: a toy that's too small is a choking hazard, and a toy that's too big is a toy your dog ignores. Measure against your dog's actual mouth, not their breed's reputation. And never leave a power chewer alone with a brand-new toy for the first hour — that's when the weak ones reveal themselves.

What Makes a Toy Suitable for Aggressive Chewers?

  • Material: Natural rubber, nylon, or reinforced materials
  • Durability rating: Look for "extreme" or "power chewer" labels
  • Size: Large enough that your dog cannot swallow it
  • No small parts: Avoid toys with squeakers that can be removed and swallowed

Top 5 Dog Toys for Aggressive Chewers

dog toys aggressive chewers

1. KONG Extreme - Best Overall

The KONG Extreme is made from ultra-durable black rubber specifically designed for power chewers. It's virtually indestructible for most dogs and can be stuffed with treats for mental stimulation. KONG Extreme is the toy I recommend most often to owners of shepherds, pits, and labs — it's the rare chew toy that survives both the jaws and the boredom.

Pros:

  • Nearly indestructible for most dogs
  • Can be stuffed with treats
  • Made in USA
  • Available in multiple sizes

2. Goughnuts MAXX - For Extreme Chewers

Designed for the most aggressive chewers, the Goughnuts MAXX features a safety indicator - when the red inner core shows through, it's time to replace the toy. It's the only chew toy I've seen with a genuine replacement guarantee, and if your dog has already destroyed a KONG Extreme, this is the next step up. Check the current price on Amazon.

3. West Paw Qwizl - Best for Treats

A durable toy that holds bully sticks and other long-lasting treats. Made from recyclable materials in the USA. West Paw's Zogoflex material is softer on the gums than hard nylon, which matters if your dog chews for hours at a time — hard nylon can wear down teeth over the long run. West Paw Qwizl on Amazon.

4. Nylabone DuraChew - Budget Option

Affordable and long-lasting. Available in various flavors that encourage chewing. Not for dogs who break off and swallow large pieces — supervise the first few chews, and swap it out the moment it wears down to a nub. See the Nylabone DuraChew on Amazon.

5. Benebone Wishbone - Flavor Favorite

Real bacon, chicken, or peanut butter flavor infused throughout. The wishbone shape makes it easy for dogs to hold. Benebone is a solid pick for moderate chewers, though most power chewers finish one in a few weeks — treat it as a fun rotation toy rather than a long-term solution.

Safety Tips

  • Always supervise your dog with new toys
  • Discard toys when pieces start coming off
  • Choose appropriately sized toys
  • Check toys regularly for damage

According to the American Veterinary Medical Association, foreign-body ingestion is one of the most common reasons dogs end up in emergency surgery, and chew toys are a frequent culprit. If your dog swallows a piece of toy and starts vomiting, loses appetite, or strains to defecate, that's a vet visit — not a wait-and-see situation.

Conclusion

dog toys aggressive chewers

For most aggressive chewers, the KONG Extreme offers the best combination of durability and versatility. For the most extreme cases, Goughnuts MAXX is nearly indestructible. Always supervise play and replace damaged toys immediately.

If your dog goes through toys faster than you can buy them, look at the root cause first — under-exercised dogs chew to burn energy. Pair a good toy with a longer walk routine and you'll often find the toys start lasting twice as long. For more on keeping your dog occupied, our guides to dog puzzle toys and slow feeders and snuffle mats for foraging enrichment cover the mental-exercise side of the equation.

title: Best Fish Tanks for Beginners 2026: Easy Setup Aquariums
description: Getting your first fish tank is exciting, but it can also be overwhelming. The right tank makes all the difference between a thriving aquarium and constant...
content:
Starting Your Fishkeeping Journey

Getting your first fish tank is exciting, but it can also be overwhelming. The right tank makes all the difference between a thriving aquarium and constant problems. We've selected the best beginner-friendly options.

Source: RSPCA (Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals): The RSPCA advises that fish tanks should be fully cycled and established for at least 4-6 weeks before adding fish to ensure stable water quality and a safe nitrogen cycle.

The biggest shift in 2026 is how much easier starter tanks have gotten. The current generation of all-in-one kits ships with proper biological filtration, adjustable LED lighting, and in several cases a heater already dialed in — the Fluval Flex and the newer Aqueon kits included. Ten years ago a "starter kit" meant a glass box, a hang-on filter, and a prayer. Now the kit does most of the setup work for you, and the remaining job is yours: cycle the tank before adding fish. If you skip that step, no kit on the shelf will save you. The RSPCA's guidance above isn't a suggestion — it's the difference between a tank that thrives and a tank that kills fish in week two.

My advice for first-timers hasn't changed: start with 10 gallons, not 5. A 5-gallon tank looks easier, but small volumes swing wildly in temperature and water chemistry, and beginners don't need that added instability. A 10-gallon with a decent filter and a heater holds stable long enough for you to learn the hobby instead of fighting it.

Beginner-Friendly Features to Look For

  • All-in-one kit: Includes filter, heater, and light
  • Appropriate size: 5-20 gallons is ideal for beginners
  • Easy maintenance: Accessible filter and feeding openings
  • LED lighting: Energy efficient and good for plants

Top 5 Fish Tanks for Beginners

fish tanks beginners

1. Fluval Flex - Best Overall

A modern all-in-one aquarium with built-in filtration and LED lighting. The curved front glass provides a beautiful view. Available in 9 and 15 gallon sizes. Fluval Flex on Amazon.

2. Aqueon LED Kit - Best Value

A complete kit at an affordable price. Includes filter, heater, LED light, and samples. Available in 10, 20, and 29 gallon sizes. For most beginners, the 20-gallon Aqueon is the sweet spot — big enough to be stable, small enough to fit on a standard desk or dresser. Aqueon LED Kit on Amazon.

3. Marineland Portrait - Small Spaces

A stylish 5-gallon tank with hidden filtration. Perfect for a betta fish or small community. Just know what you're signing up for: 5 gallons means weekly water changes you can't skip, because there's no buffer. Marineland Portrait on Amazon.

4. Fluval Spec - For Bettas

Available in 2.5 and 5 gallon sizes with built-in filtration. Ideal for betta fish or shrimp tanks. If you're keeping a betta, check out our betta tank guide for the full setup rundown.

5. Tetra Complete Kit - Budget Choice

An affordable starter kit with everything needed. Good for learning the basics. It's the kit I'd point a kid or a student toward — it won't wow you, but it teaches the routine without the price tag.

Essential Equipment Checklist

  • Filter: Matched to tank size
  • Heater: 50-100 watts for most tanks
  • Thermometer: Monitor water temperature
  • Water conditioner: Remove chlorine
  • Test kit: Monitor ammonia, nitrite, nitrate

The one piece of equipment I'd never skip is a liquid test kit. Test strips are fine for a quick glance, but when you're cycling a new tank you need real ammonia and nitrite numbers, and only liquid reagents give you those. Our water test kit guide breaks down what's worth owning, and our nitrogen cycle guide walks through the cycling process week by week.

The RSPCA also flags overfeeding as one of the leading causes of poor water quality in home aquariums — uneaten food rots and spikes ammonia, which then stresses or kills fish. The fix is dull, but it works: feed a small amount once or twice a day, and if food is still floating after two minutes, you've fed too much. Tie feeding to a routine rather than eyeballing it.

Beginner Fish Recommendations

fish tanks beginners

  • Betta fish: Hardy, beautiful, can live alone
  • Guppies: Colorful and easy to care for
  • Tetras: Peaceful schooling fish
  • Corydoras: Bottom dwellers, help clean

Conclusion

For most beginners, the Fluval Flex offers the best combination of features and ease of use. The Aqueon LED Kit provides excellent value. Start with at least 5 gallons - smaller tanks are actually harder to maintain.

And once the tank is running, resist the urge to add fish fast. Add two or three at a time, wait two weeks, then add more. The bacteria in your filter can only handle so much waste at once, and every new fish is a new load on the system. A little patience here prevents most of the beginner disasters you read about on forums. For food recommendations once your fish are in, see our aquarium fish food guide.

title: Best Hamster Cages 2026
description: Most store-bought hamster cages are too small. Hamsters are active animals that need space to run, burrow, and explore. A cage that's too small leads to...
content:
Why Cage Size Matters for Hamsters

Most store-bought hamster cages are too small. Hamsters are active animals that need space to run, burrow, and explore. A cage that's too small leads to stress, boredom, and health problems.

Source: RSPCA (Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals): The RSPCA recommends a minimum of 100 x 50cm (approximately 775 square inches) of continuous floor space for a hamster, with larger always being better. Most commercial cages marketed for hamsters fall far below this.

If there's one thing that changed in 2026, it's that the "big cage" movement won. The old 10-gallon aquarium and the classic tube-filled starter kits are now widely understood to be too small for any hamster, and the community standard has moved to what used to be called "bin cages" — large, deep plastic bins or 40-gallon-plus aquariums with 8–10 inches of bedding. Hamsters are burrowing animals first and everything else second. A Syrian needs enough bedding depth to dig a full burrow system, and the modern advice is simple: floor space and bedding depth beat every fancy feature a cage can offer.

That's also why the Midwest Critter Nation keeps winning our top slot — it delivers the floor space and the deep base pan in one package. If you're sizing a cage for the first time, aim for at least 450 square inches of continuous floor space for a Syrian and 360 for a dwarf, and remember that every wheel, house, and dish you add takes usable floor space away from the hamster.

Minimum Cage Size Requirements

  • Syrian Hamsters: Minimum 450 square inches of floor space
  • Dwarf Hamsters: Minimum 360 square inches of floor space
  • Height: At least 12 inches for bedding depth

Top 5 Hamster Cages

hamster cages

1. Midwest Critter Nation - Best Overall

A spacious wire cage with wide doors for easy access. The deep pan holds plenty of bedding. Easy to clean and highly rated by owners. Midwest Critter Nation on Amazon.

2. Savic Hamster Heaven - Complete Setup

Comes with accessories included: wheel, house, water bottle, and food dish. Ready for immediate use. It's a solid first cage — just be aware the included wheel may need upgrading to a larger, solid-surface model for a Syrian. Savic Hamster Heaven on Amazon.

3. Prevue Hendryx - Budget Option

Affordable wire cage with a deep plastic base. Good ventilation and easy cleaning. One of the few budget cages that clears the 450-square-inch bar for a Syrian, which is why it makes the list. Prevue Hendryx on Amazon.

4. IKEA Detolf - DIY Option

A glass display cabinet turned on its side makes an excellent large hamster home. Requires DIY modification. It's cheap and enormous — roughly 930 square inches — but you'll need a custom lid and some patience with the assembly. Our hamster cage setup guide covers the modification steps.

5. Kaytee CritterTrail - Expandable

Connect multiple units with tubes to create a larger habitat. Best for dwarf hamsters. Honest note: tubes are fun to watch, but they're corridors, not living space — a CritterTrail on its own is too small for any hamster. Use it as an add-on to a properly sized main cage, or skip it entirely. See our full hamster cage roundup for more options.

Essential Accessories

  • Wheel: 8-12 inches, solid surface (no wire)
  • Hideout: For sleeping and security
  • Water bottle: 4-8 oz capacity
  • Bedding: Paper-based or aspen (no cedar or pine)

What to Avoid

hamster cages

  • Wire floors (cause foot problems)
  • Cedar or pine bedding (respiratory issues)
  • Small cages under 360 sq inches
  • Wheels with gaps (leg injuries)

On bedding: the Humane Society of the United States and most exotic vets are aligned on this — avoid cedar and pine shavings entirely. The aromatic oils they release are linked to respiratory and liver problems in small mammals. Paper-based bedding or aspen shavings are the safe, absorbent choices, and our hamster bedding guide goes into the details.

Conclusion

The Midwest Critter Nation offers the best value and space. For a complete starter kit, Savic Hamster Heaven includes everything you need. Always prioritize floor space over fancy features.

If you're on a budget, skip the fancy kits and build a bin cage — a large storage bin, a mesh lid, and 10 inches of paper bedding costs less than $60 and beats most commercial cages on floor space. It's the best value in hamster keeping, and it's the setup most experienced owners end up recommending anyway. For the full picture on wheels, tunnels, and accessories, check our hamster wheel guide and tunnel systems guide.

title: Best Rabbit Food 2026
description: Rabbits have unique dietary needs: unlimited hay, the right pellets, and fresh greens. This guide covers the best rabbit foods and how to build a complete diet.
content:
Best Rabbit Food 2026: Complete Nutrition Guide for Your Bunny

Rabbits have unique dietary requirements that differ significantly from other pets. A proper diet is essential for their dental health, digestive function, and overall well-being. This guide covers the best rabbit foods available and how to build a complete diet for your bunny.

Source: House Rabbit Society (HRS): The House Rabbit Society recommends that adult rabbits receive unlimited access to grass hay (timothy, orchard, or brome), a measured daily portion of high-fiber pellets, and a daily serving of fresh leafy greens. Hay should make up roughly 80% of the diet — pellets are a supplement, not the foundation.

The 2026 update here is real, not cosmetic. More rabbit owners than ever are keeping their bunnies on a hay-first diet, and the pellet brands that matter have responded: fiber minimums have crept up across the board, and the better lines now publish guaranteed analysis numbers you can actually verify on the bag. Oxbow and Small Pet Select both sit at 22–25% fiber, which is where you want to be. Anything under 18% is a red flag — that pellet is mostly filler, and rabbits on low-fiber diets end up with GI stasis, dental disease, and obesity.

One more thing worth saying plainly: muesli-style mixes with colorful pieces, seeds, and corn are still sold everywhere, and they're still a bad idea. Rabbits will pick out the sweet bits and leave the nutritionally dense pellets behind, which is exactly how you get a fat rabbit with bad teeth. If your rabbit currently eats muesli, switching to a uniform pellet takes a week or two of gradual mixing — and it's one of the highest-impact changes you can make.

Quick Comparison: Top Rabbit Foods

ProductFiberProteinBest For
Oxbow Essentials Adult Rabbit Food22-25%14%Best overall, widely available
Small Pet Select Rabbit Food22-25%14%Premium, small-batch, picky eaters
Kaytee Forti-Diet Pro Health18-20%14%Budget-friendly, fortified
Burgess Excel Adult Rabbit Nuggets19%14%Nugget format prevents selective feeding

Understanding Rabbit Nutrition

The Rabbit Diet Pyramid

  • 80% — Unlimited grass hay (timothy, orchard, brome)
  • 10-15% — Fresh leafy greens
  • 5-10% — High-fiber pellets

Hay is non-negotiable. Rabbits need unlimited access to fresh hay (grass hay like timothy) for:

  • Dental health (wears down constantly growing teeth)
  • Digestive health (high fiber keeps gut moving)
  • Mental stimulation

Rabbits' teeth grow continuously — roughly 3-5mm per month for the incisors — and hay is the abrasive they need to keep them worn down. Without it, you're looking at malocclusion, abscesses, and expensive vet dentistry. The House Rabbit Society estimates that dental disease is among the most common health problems in pet rabbits, and the vast majority of it traces back to inadequate hay intake.

What to Look for in Rabbit Pellets

NutrientIdeal AmountWhy It Matters
Fiber18-22%+Essential for digestion
Protein12-14% (adults)Growth and maintenance
Fat1-3%Energy
Calcium0.4-0.6%Prevents urinary issues

Red Flags to Avoid

  • Seeds and nuts (choking hazard, too fatty)
  • Colorful pieces (artificial dyes)
  • High sugar content
  • Low fiber (<18%)
  • Corn-based ingredients

1. Oxbow Essentials Adult Rabbit Food - Best Overall

Rating: 5/5

Why We Love It

Oxbow is the benchmark that other rabbit pellets are measured against. Timothy-based, 22-25% fiber, no seeds, no dyes, and it's stocked at virtually every pet store in North America — which matters more than you'd think, because a sudden diet switch when your regular brand disappears is a recipe for GI upset.

Key Features

  • Fiber: 22-25%
  • Protein: 14%
  • Type: Timothy hay-based
  • Made in USA

Pros

  • Vet-recommended standard
  • Consistent, no cheap fillers
  • Widely available in all sizes

Cons

  • Pricier than grocery-store brands

Best For

Most adult rabbits. If you only remember one name from this article, make it this one. Oxbow Essentials Adult Rabbit Food on Amazon.

2. Small Pet Select Rabbit Food - Premium Choice

Rating: 5/5

Why We Love It

Small Pet Select is a family-owned company that sources high-quality ingredients from local farms. Their timothy hay-based pellets are fresh and highly palatable — the freshness is the selling point, because pellets that sat in a warehouse for a year lose both aroma and nutrients.

Key Features

  • Fiber: 22-25%
  • Protein: 14%
  • Type: Timothy hay-based
  • Made in USA

Pros

  • Fresh, high-quality ingredients

  • Small batch production
  • Excellent for picky eaters

Cons

Owners who want premium quality and are willing to pay more. Great for picky rabbits. Small Pet Select Rabbit Food on Amazon.

3. Kaytee Forti-Diet Pro Health Rabbit Food - Budget Option

Rating: 4.5/5

Why We Love It

Kaytee Forti-Diet is the reliable budget pick. It hits 18-20% fiber, includes added probiotics and prebiotics for digestive support, and undercuts the premium brands by a solid margin. It's not the highest-fiber option on the shelf, but for most healthy adult rabbits it's perfectly adequate — and it's sold just about everywhere.

Key Features

  • Fiber: 18-20%
  • Protein: 14%
  • Type: Timothy-based, fortified

Pros

  • Affordable
  • Added probiotics
  • Widely available

Cons

The Complete Rabbit Diet

Daily Requirements for Adult Rabbits

Food TypeAmountNotes
Grass hayUnlimitedTimothy, orchard, or brome; 80% of the diet
Pellets1/4 cup per 5 lbsHigh-fiber, uniform pellet only
Fresh greens1-2 cups per 5 lbsLeafy greens: romaine, cilantro, parsley, kale in moderation
WaterUnlimitedFresh daily, bowl preferred over bottle

Feeding Guidelines by Age

Baby Rabbits (0-6 months)

  • Hay: Alfalfa hay (higher calcium for growing)
  • Pellets: Unlimited alfalfa-based pellets
  • Veggies: Introduce slowly at 3 months

Young Rabbits (6 months - 1 year)

  • Hay: Transition from alfalfa to timothy
  • Pellets: Reduce to 1/2 cup per 5 lbs
  • Veggies: Introduce more variety

Adult Rabbits (1+ years)

  • Hay: Timothy or grass hay (unlimited)
  • Pellets: 1/4 cup per 5 lbs
  • Veggies: 1-2 cups per 5 lbs

Senior Rabbits (7+ years)

  • Same as adults, but monitor weight
  • May need more protein if losing weight
  • Consult vet for specific needs

Our Verdict

For the best overall nutrition, Oxbow Essentials Adult Rabbit Food combined with unlimited timothy hay and fresh vegetables is the ideal diet for most adult rabbits. If you want premium quality and your rabbit is picky, Small Pet Select is worth the extra cost.

Remember: Pellets are only a small part of the diet. Unlimited hay is the foundation of rabbit health!

Whatever you feed, introduce any new food gradually over 7-10 days — rabbits have sensitive digestive systems, and a sudden switch is one of the most common triggers for GI stasis, which is genuinely life-threatening. If your rabbit stops eating or stops producing droppings, that's an emergency: get to a rabbit-savvy vet the same day.
